Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):  Acute episodic left-sided throbbing headache with visual aura, nausea/vomiting; clinician impression of migraine. No chronic diseases reported.  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):  Mother—migraine and hypothyroidism. No family history of brain cancer reported.  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:  Microgynon combined oral contraceptive pill, dose/route/frequency not documented; intermittent use of unspecified “painkillers” previously (names/doses not documented).  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):  Not recorded.  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks:  Uses COC for contraception; no additional sexual history recorded.  
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:  No smoking; no alcohol; no regular exercise; high job stress; no substance use recorded.  
- Hearing and vision concerns:  Reports transient blurred vision and zig-zag visual aura preceding headache; photophobia (wearing sunglasses). Hearing concerns not recorded.  
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm):  Reports significant health anxiety about brain cancer; feels stressed but denies low mood; no self-harm ideation recorded.  
- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors:  Lives alone; works in high-pressure fashion industry; workplace stress noted; otherwise coping.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: Acute unilateral throbbing headache with visual aura, photophobia, nausea/vomiting; no focal neurologic deficits; similar episode weeks ago; recent initiation of estrogen-containing OCP; high stress levels.  
- Working diagnosis: Migraine with visual aura—supported by classic symptom cluster, positive maternal history, and absence of red-flag neurologic signs.  
- Differential considerations:  
  • Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST)—medium likelihood given new severe headache, positional worsening, and estrogen OCP use; no focal deficits but low threshold for imaging if symptoms escalate.  
  • Intracranial mass/tumor—low likelihood; acute, non-progressive course argues against but remain vigilant if headaches become persistent or progressive.  
- Management today:  
  • Symptomatic treatment—analgesia: paracetamol, co-codamol, and/or NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen); specific doses not documented.  
  • Advice to maintain headache diary to identify triggers/frequency.  
  • Safety-netting: return urgently for worsening headache, lack of response to medication, new neurologic symptoms, or visual changes.  
  • Follow-up appointment arranged for next week to review response and consider prophylactic migraine therapy if attacks persist.  

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  Discussed stress management, adequate rest, and potential benefit of regular exercise; encouraged use of headache diary.  
- Patient health goals and priorities:  Relief of headache symptoms; reassurance regarding cancer fears; ability to return to work.  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA):  Not recorded.  
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports):  None initiated today; consider psychology/stress-management resources if headaches linked to stress.  
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled:  Review in 1 week; sooner if red-flag symptoms emerge.  

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral:  Consider if ongoing health anxiety or work-related stress persists.  
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management:  Consider neurology referral if headache frequency increases, atypical features develop, or concern for CVST persists.  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified:  Not recorded.  
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening:  Consider if visual auras change or persist.  
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected:  Not recorded.  
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health:  Not recorded.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Migraine with visual aura – High likelihood: Unilateral throbbing headache, pre-monitory zig-zag visual aura, photophobia, nausea/vomiting, familial migraine history, and absence of neurologic deficits.  
2. Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis – Medium likelihood: New severe headache worsened on leaning forward plus recent estrogen OCP use; may mimic migraine.  
3. Intracranial mass/tumor – Low likelihood: Positional headache and vomiting raise possibility, but acute, non-progressive pattern and normal neurologic review make this less probable.

● Internal conflicts or contradictions: None noted between transcript and DDx.
